target.statement: A finite cover of a compact connected metric space by closed bounded-length visibility regions contains an overlapping pair, yielding a path between two anchors of length at most the sum of their budgets.

recommended_name.attribution: For the closedness step cite Burago--Burago--Ivanov, Theorem 2.5.14 and Proposition 2.5.19; for the overlap step say simply 'by connectedness' or 'the intersection graph of a finite closed cover of a connected space is connected'.

sources.citation: D. Burago, Y. Burago, and S. Ivanov, A Course in Metric Geometry, Graduate Studies in Mathematics 33, American Mathematical Society, 2001
exact_locators: Theorem 2.5.14, printed p. 48: uniformly length-bounded curves in a compact metric space have a uniformly convergent subsequence
Proposition 2.5.19, printed pp. 49--50: a rectifiably connected pair in a compact metric space has a shortest path, using lower semicontinuity of length
sources.relationship: These results make the induced extended length distance attain finite values and make its finite sublevel balls closed in the original compact topology.
sources.claim_boundary: The text does not state the visibility terminology, the finite-cover consumer, or the lemniscate reduction.

sources.citation: The defining separation characterization of connectedness
sources.exact_locator: A connected space has no partition into two nonempty disjoint clopen subsets.
sources.relationship: If the intersection graph of a finite nonempty closed cover were disconnected, the unions over its two vertex classes would be disjoint nonempty closed complements, hence a separation.
sources.claim_boundary: This is foundational topology rather than a literature-sensitive theorem requiring an eponym.

mechanism_comparison.intrinsic_ball_reformulation: Let d_L be the extended length distance on X. Proposition 2.5.19 shows that whenever d_L(x,a_j) is finite it is attained, so V_j={x:d_L(x,a_j)<=r_j}; bounded-curve compactness and lower semicontinuity make this sublevel closed.
mechanism_comparison.cover_consumer: The proof needs only that a finite nonempty closed cover of a connected space has connected intersection graph; one edge gives the desired pair.
mechanism_comparison.budget_additivity: Concatenating the two witness curves is exactly the triangle inequality for d_L and gives r_i+r_j.
mechanism_comparison.application_delta: The lemniscate reduction uses the overlap consumer to turn a one-root intrinsic cover into the required two-root path, then the minimum-enclosing-disk normalization makes the final inequality strict.
